svg.title: crosslemma: how a claim becomes a result
svg.desc: The crosslemma cycle in five lanes (you, the orchestrator, sandboxed runs, computed, the record): a brief passes your first approval gate, a sandboxed solver produces claims, a checker script and fresh referees certify them, the earned tag is computed, and your second approval appends it to the append-only claims ledger. Below, the four mechanisms: the approval gate, the hook and sandbox, the record, packets and outside input.
svg.text: crosslemmaa workspace kit for working on open mathematics problems with AI agents
Nothing becomes a result until something other than its author has checked it, and you approve every launch and every ledger entry.
The rule underneath: whoever produced the work does not get to certify it.
bin/manifest lists every file the worker

and the exact flags. You approve those

exactly these claim ids and their bytes.

It runs bin/close-run: check + merge + verdict table; launches and appends nothing.

Not a defence against your own account: the gates stop agents' misreadings and mistakes, not a deliberate forgery. See SECURITY.md.
